title: Surviving Whammies
summary:
Surviving Whammies
US refiners are being forced to deal with dismal margins brought about by a lack of demand for their prime products - gasoline and diesel. Consumption of gasoline is roughly 7 percent less than the go‐go days of mid‐2007 - and once the growth in ethanol use is considered, the need for refiners' hydrocarbon component has contracted even more. Diesel use has evaporated by some one million barrels per day (mbd) or over 20 percent from its highs of late 2007.

children.title: Motor Gasoline
children.summary: Distillate Fuel Oil Over the last few years, the cumulative impact of lower product demand and greater mandated use of biofuels has raised the level of idle US refining capacity. Even when the recently announced closures of the Sunoco New Jersey and Valero Delaware refineries are reflected in operable capacity, the capacity glut remains above the levels of just a few years ago unless more refinery closures occur.

children.title: Refinery Inputs
children.summary: Refinery Operable Capacity Idle Capacity The Renewable Fuel Standard dictates that by 2022 the inclusion of biofuels in gasoline must increase nearly three‐fold from 2009's mandated level of 11.1 billion gallons per year (685 kbd). Faced with the prospect of over 1.3 mbd additional biofuel being included in gasoline as well as improving vehicle fleet fuel efficiency, a US refiner may see little reason to expand their ability to produce more hydrocarbon‐based fuel.

children.title: The Coup de grâce?
children.summary: US rules on limiting domestic GHG emissions are still wending their way through the legislative process. But judging by the volume of complaints emanating from segments of the refining industry, one might conclude that the rules proposed by the country's august legislators are less than fair and equitable to all parties affected.

children.title: GHG Legislation Forming, Tanker Owners Take Warning
section_path: GHG Legislation Forming, Tanker Owners Take Warning
children.section_path_text: GHG Legislation Forming, Tanker Owners Take Warning
children.summary: The seemingly endless line of storm clouds gathering around US refiners does not appear to bode well for people trying to make a living carrying crude oil to the shores of this nation. While domestic refining capacity in a few niche markets may weather the pending GHG allocation storm, some of those located in markets with easy access to imports may become pressured financially and eventually succumb.
